chemical_assumptions: No chemistry modules are enabled. Only element/geometry proxies are used: terminal elements C,C,N are treated as element labels, not as asserted early-state chemical roles. The pocket sites (VAL53:CG1, MET163:CE, HIS160:CE1, HIS160:NE2) are used as geometric reference points only; no protonation, charge, or tautomer state is assumed. The orientation triplet [15,4,14] is used as a geometric orientation constraint, not as a chemical interaction claim.
clock_and_representation: Clock policy is fixed: observable is predictive_bridge_to_learning_end, teacher is actual_ancestor_at_learning_end. The ancestor record provides actual current world A coordinates at current_clock_times [0.0, 0.12, 0.25, 0.5] and same-forward teacher predicted endpoint world A coordinates. Current versus endpoint targets must not be exchanged. The selection_trend uses weights from score_time applied to proposal at state_time, with proposal beyond the learning window excluded. The controller_response is the measured current-program response (R19_v2 parent, R15_V3_COMPATIBLE actual program) with no extra inference and no terminal-affinity gradient.
falsifier: Falsified if: (a) point_rms_A does not decrease toward the teacher endpoint within the window, or atom_clip_fraction/cumulative_clip_fraction become nonzero indicating dose saturation; (b) the local geometry forms but terminal affinity tail does not improve (n_above_target stays 0 and U_tau does not exceed parent 0.0091), which would replicate the prior finding that local identity formation is not sufficient for affinity benefit; (c) the focal trace deviates from 1.0 or realized_selection_shift grows to dominate native_shift, indicating the mode is not actually selection-enriched.
formation_retention_value_test: Formation test: does the C,C,N local geometry form at the matched slots within the learning window, measured by decreasing point_rms_A toward the teacher endpoint and nonzero active_updates? Retention test: after the window closes and native completion runs to 1, is the formed local geometry retained (final point_rms_A not reverting) and does the terminal candidate remain qualified (n_qualified, best_qualified_pic50)? Value test: does the intervention improve the terminal affinity tail (n_above_target, U_tau) relative to the parent outcomes (n_above_target 0, U_tau 0.0091, best_qualified_pic50 8.590) rather than only improving local geometry?
observable_change: Expected observable: point_rms_A and target_error_mean decrease over the active window as the matched slots approach the teacher predicted endpoint; injected_rms_A_mean stays near the requested ~0.03 A with atom_clip_fraction and cumulative_clip_fraction at 0.0; assignment_switch_fraction remains low (parent mean ~0.016). The local focal trace should remain 1.0 and the realized_selection_shift should stay small relative to native_shift. No affinity-head gradient is expected; terminal pIC50 change is a downstream readout, not a direct observable of this intervention.
relationship_to_failed_families: Prior campaign (local_motif20_v2_20261015) found that local identity formation (e.g., terminal N geometry match) did not equal affinity benefit, and that tighter point-cloud fitting was not the primary gap. The same element matching cost used on 3-point N/C regions (R16) or 4-point O regions (R18) did not replicate the benefit seen with wider 20/25-point support, indicating support-background dependence. This hypothesis is a narrower 3-point C,C,N support, so it is at risk of the same failure mode; the falsifier explicitly tests whether local formation translates to terminal affinity tail improvement. The prior campaign also noted limited exploration coverage and anchoring on F_b011_s030, which this handoff does not resolve.
scientific_hypothesis: The interface15 local support (atom slots [4,14,15], terminal elements C,C,N, orientation triplet [15,4,14]) is a selection-enriched local geometry mode: the focal trace is exactly 1.0 at all sampled times with zero RMSE, while the background mean stays near 1.0 and the expected/realized selection shifts are small (order 1e-4 to 1e-2 A). This indicates the mode is a stable, near-deterministic local identity rather than a noisy background fluctuation. The hypothesis is that steering this 3-point C,C,N support toward the same-forward teacher predicted endpoint (teacher_time 0.5, window [0.1,0.5]) will move the local geometry in the intended direction without requiring an affinity-head gradient, and that any terminal-affinity benefit is mediated by the local geometry change, not by direct logit/element forcing (assignment_element_cost 0.5 is detached).
support_reason: Interface15 is the only queried candidate with a 3-point support and an orientation triplet, and its selection_trend shows a focal trace of exactly 1.0 with zero RMSE across all sampled times, indicating a stable selection-enriched local mode rather than a noisy background. The ancestor record confirms the selected support [4,14,15] with terminal elements C,C,N and provides both actual current and same-forward teacher predicted endpoint coordinates, enabling a fixed-clock predictive-bridge observable. The controller_response confirms the actual program (R15_V3_COMPATIBLE) has coordinate_updates_only true, affinity_head_gradient false, and detached sensing, so the intervention is geometry-only and does not directly force elements or logits.
